scenario_summary: Misleading wording: the whitepaper markets 'bank-grade encryption... to the highest industry standard' without specifying any algorithm or protocol, while the technical questionnaire elsewhere reveals TLS 1.0 (a deprecated, known-weak protocol) is still supported on customer-facing endpoints. The marketing claim, read against the technical detail, is actively misleading rather than merely vague.

claims.subject: overall encryption standard
claims.source_excerpt: Vantree protects customer data with bank-grade encryption at every layer of our platform, giving customers confidence that their data is secured to the highest industry standard.
claims.evidence_requirement: Technical detail (specific protocols/algorithms in use) consistent with the implied claim of top-tier, current encryption practice across the platform.

evidence_items.excerpt: For backward compatibility with certain legacy enterprise clients, Vantree supports TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.2 on customer-facing endpoints. TLS 1.0 support is scheduled for deprecation in a future release.

claims.expected_handling_notes: 'Bank-grade encryption... highest industry standard' is unverifiable as a standalone phrase (it names no standard), but the questionnaire's own technical detail reveals TLS 1.0 — a protocol version deprecated industry-wide for known weaknesses — is still actively supported. Read together, the marketing language is misleading rather than merely vague: it implies a standard the vendor's own more specific disclosure contradicts. Distinguish from case-05, where vague language was genuinely compatible with the more specific claim; here the more specific claim actively undercuts the vague one.

claims.subject: encryption at rest
claims.source_excerpt: Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
claims.evidence_requirement: None beyond the questionnaire itself in this package.

evidence_items.excerpt: Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.

claims.expected_handling_notes: At-rest encryption itself is not implicated in the TLS-in-transit issue found in c1 — the two should not be conflated.
